title: Post’s functional completeness criterion

based_on.title: Post’s Functional Completeness Theorem
based_on.pages: 463–475 (five classes and elementary completeness proof; nullary term convention made explicit)

summary: Characterize complete Boolean bases by five composition-preserved restrictions, then construct negation, constants and conjunction from explicit witnesses.
abstract: NAND can express every truth table when an input is available, whereas exclusive or and negation together cannot express conjunction. A general criterion explains the difference. Five simple restrictions on truth tables survive every composition: preserving zero, preserving one, monotonicity, reversing outputs when all inputs are reversed, and dependence only on a parity of selected inputs. A basis expresses every positive-input truth function exactly when its operations escape each restriction. The proof constructs negation, constant-valued terms and conjunction from those failures. Representing truth functions with no inputs needs one additional ingredient: a genuine closed term, rather than a term that still mentions an input while ignoring its value.
